summary: New component envoy-infra:gcp:ClusteredNatsHub in packages/envoy/infra/gcp: the official NATS chart 2.15.1 through a Pulumi helm v4 Chart (three pods, one per zone, a PVC each, JetStream clustered, reloader, exporter), users rendered by core.Authorization.Render into an included auth.conf, a session-user annotation that rolls the pods, a NetworkPolicy, a GMP PodMonitoring, and an optional tailnet block (two or more pods, each a userspace Tailscale host of one Tailscale Service plus the session listener on loopback and a health-gated advertiser). The component builds its own Kubernetes provider with mutable ConfigMaps and protects the StatefulSet. Proof: mock unit tests, a helm-template render test of the vendored chart, and three local nats-server 2.15.1 processes with the real reloader and exporter. Merges after INFRA-546.

implement: legion-worker: phase rules, the proof object, the PR body (references/pr-body.md), bringing main in (references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md) and the tools reference for go install of helm, nats-server, the reloader and the exporter

envoy: messaging the architect and siblings (INFRA-546, INFRA-550, INFRA-557, INFRA-560 coordination) over Envoy
asd-ste100: the PR body and every message to the architect and other roles
test: legion-worker: the tester's proof objects, re-running 4.4's first three rows at the head and the negative controls
envoy: questions to the implementer or architect over Envoy
review: legion-worker: the review and merge gate (references/merge-gate.md, references/review-threads.md) and the no-deferral rule

findings.finding: Two stacks would own the in-cluster Service envoy-hub (agent-infra bridge Service vs the component's).
findings.answer: The component creates the client Service under the serviceName input and also outputs podSelector, so INFRA-553 can take the name or retarget envoy-cluster's Service; sent to the architect (plan 1.2, 5.B).

findings.finding: Session-listener pods started before the move would create the stream, KV buckets and durable the restore needs; the new listener must keep the VM's machine id, user and seed.
findings.answer: tailnet block is optional and the hub deploys without it; recommendation to the architect that INFRA-553 adds it after the restore; machineId defaults to the Tailscale Service name (envoy-hub) and the listener user is named after it with ListenerPermissions, as on the VM (plan 2.4, 2.6, 5.A, 5.D).

findings.finding: Pods that advertise before the Tailscale Service exists stay unapproved.
findings.answer: Auto-advertisement off; the advertiser advertises explicitly, marks the pod ready only when the service-host capability lists the Service, and drains and re-advertises after 120 s unapproved (broker recovery); README requires the Service first (plan 2.4).

findings.finding: The tailnet entry and the session listener are effectively one workload.
findings.answer: One Deployment, one budget; each pod a Tailscale host serving 4222 and 9020, matching spec v2's contract (plan 2.4).

findings.finding: ConfigMap data changes force replacement under pulumi-kubernetes defaults; StatefulSet force-new fields would take all pods down.
findings.answer: The component builds its provider from a kubeconfig input with enableConfigMapMutable and SSA; the chart's StatefulSet is protected by a transform, with disk-growth and teardown steps in the README (plan 2.2, 2.3).

findings.finding: Mocks can only pin chart values; natsBox renders a Deployment with no budget or priority class; chart source and sidecar images need pinning.
findings.answer: Values pinned on mocks plus a natslive render test with helm v3.20.2 against the vendored chart archive checked by its index SHA-256; natsBox off; every image a digest input; chart repo/name/version constants (plan 2.1, 4.1, 4.2).

findings.finding: Nothing in the chart rolls the pods only when the session user changes; no acceptance covers a rejected no_auth_user reload.
findings.answer: Annotation from the session user's key alone; mock test that other user changes leave the pod template alone; local test shows the session change rejected on reload and taken after restart (plan 2.7, 4.1, 4.3).

findings.finding: The three-local-servers acceptance cannot run as written (pod names, paths; in-process server is 2.10.29; CI runs natslive only in core and seed).
findings.answer: nats-server 2.15.1 binaries via go install, run on the chart-rendered config with per-process command-line overrides; CI line gains ./gcp/ (plan 4.3, task 8, departure 2).

findings.finding: The exporter has no current-copies metric; PodMonitoring is not in the root's grant ask.
findings.answer: Copies counted as servers reporting a stream, current when last_seq equals the stream's highest; local test proves the series and names; PodMonitoring grant sent to the architect (plan 2.8, 5.C).

findings.finding: The network policy misses the exporter port; route authentication undecided.
findings.answer: 7777 admitted from metricsNamespaces (default GMP namespaces); routes protected by the NetworkPolicy alone, stated in docs (plan 2.1, 2.5).

findings.finding: Before INFRA-557 lands a second listener pod crash-loops; Tailscale routing does not follow readiness.
findings.answer: The component's replica count is an input with minimum 2 and does not depend on 557's code; the advertiser withdraws an unhealthy host; 557's readiness contract sent to the architect (plan 2.4, 5.F).

findings.finding: Session-listener settings depend on unmerged siblings (ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS, INFRA-546's byte limit).
findings.answer: core.ListenerConfig gains NATSReplicas and StreamMaxBytes, rendered only when set; spec v3 makes both inputs; this PR merges after INFRA-546 (plan 2.9, 2.10, task 0, 5.E).

findings.finding: Reuse and inputs the spec does not list; overlap with INFRA-560; #2283 not in the base.
findings.answer: Shared users builder with gcp:NatsHub; full input list in 1.1; Kubernetes Secret by reference for the seed; outputs in 1.2; tailnet-host pieces in gcp/tailnet_service.go for INFRA-560; main brought in at task 0 (plan 1, 2.4, 2.6).

findings.finding: JetStream limits differ from the VM's; file store as large as the disk leaves no headroom.
findings.answer: max_file_store below the disk with defaults and refusals derived from INFRA-546's byte limit and measurements (plan 1.1).

findings.finding: Acceptance lines no machine can check (metrics enough for alerts, release, docs, no-restart reload under Kubernetes).
findings.answer: Local exporter test for the metric basis; release checked by the production check via the GitHub release and get-schema; docs read by the reviewer; the live reload and roll are INFRA-551/552's (plan 4.3, 4.4).

specDepartures.spec: NATS's client port only from the namespaces named as inputs.
specDepartures.plan: Also from the component's own tailnet pods by pod selector, since they forward the tailnet's 4222.
specDepartures.evidence: The tailnet pods forward TCP 4222 to the in-cluster Service; gcp:Dispatch admits its own front-door pod the same way (packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_kube.go:548-550 at a2a6afc9).

specDepartures.spec: The rendered NATS configuration is run by three local nats-server processes.
specDepartures.plan: The chart-rendered nats.conf and auth.conf, with command-line overrides for each process's ports, routes, store directory, PID file and server name.
specDepartures.evidence: The chart renders server_name from $SERVER_NAME, pid_file /var/run/nats/nats.pid, store_dir /data and routes to <statefulset>-<i>.<headless>:6222 (chart nats-2.15.1 files/config/config.yaml, cluster.yaml, jetstream.yaml), which no local process can use as written.

# INFRA-549 plan: `envoy-infra:gcp:ClusteredNatsHub`

Issue: dispatch://INFRA-549 (spec v3: v2 added the tailnet-policy contract, every host of the Tailscale Service carries `tag:envoy-hub-host` and serves TCP 4222 and TCP 9020; v3 added the replica-count and byte-limit inputs, sizing from INFRA-546's numbers and INFRA-546's bucket update grant). Root: dispatch://INFRA-14 (approved v11), items 1, 3, 5, 6, 9, 11. Repository: sjawhar/legion. Running system for this child (spec): envoy-infra's Go tests and local nats-server processes; the live proof on the cluster is dispatch://INFRA-551's.

## 1. What gets built

One new component in `packages/envoy/infra/gcp`, token `envoy-infra:gcp:ClusteredNatsHub`, Go type `ClusteredNatsHub`, constructor `NewClusteredNatsHub`, registered in `provider/provider.go` beside `gcp:NatsHub`. It is in package `gcp` because it uses GKE-only pieces (Google Managed Prometheus `PodMonitoring`, Autopilot floors) and reuses that package's rules (`imageRule`, `tagRule`, `hostnameRule`, `tailnetDNSNameRule`, `namespaceRule`, `secretKeyRule`, `appQuantity`, `refuseSeed*`, the NetworkPolicy helpers `podPeer`/`ingressFrom`/`policy` in `dispatch_kube.go:514-560` at base a2a6afc9, the `gcp:NatsUser` and `gcp:SessionUser` types). Cluster facts are inputs. Line numbers below are at base a2a6afc9; task 0 shifts some.

### 1.1 Inputs (plain unless marked)

| Input | Rule |
|---|---|
| `kubeconfig` | `pulumi.StringInput`, `provider:"secret"`, required. Checked once it resolves: blank or whitespace-only refused, nkey seed refused (as `gcp:Dispatch` does for its secrets). The component builds its own `kubernetes.Provider` `<name>-kubernetes` from it with `EnableServerSideApply: true` and `EnableConfigMapMutable: true` (see 2.2). |
| `namespace` | required; `namespaceRule`; the namespace must exist (not created). |
| `name` | required; DNS-1123 label of at most 44 bytes, so `<name>-tailnet` stays within the 52-byte StatefulSet/Deployment name limit the controller-revision-hash label needs. Becomes the chart's `fullnameOverride` and release name. |
| `serviceName` | required; DNS-1035 label: the in-cluster client Service (the chart's `service.name`). |
| `natsImage`, `reloaderImage`, `exporterImage` | required; `imageRule` (pinned by digest). Defaults are not given: the consumer pins `mirror.gcr.io/library/nats:2.15.1-alpine@sha256:…`, the reloader 0.24.0 and exporter 0.20.2 images by digest (chart 2.15.1 `values.yaml:330,415,442`). |
| `natsReplicas` | `*int`, optional, 1 to 3 (the hub has three servers; JetStream refuses more copies than servers): rendered as the session listener's `ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS`, unset unless given (spec v3). |
| `streamMaxBytes` | `*int`, optional, ≥ 1: rendered as the session listener's `ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES` (dispatch://INFRA-546's setting, `plan-md` decision 7), unset unless given (spec v3); it also sizes the disk and memory below. |
| `maxFileStoreGb` | `*int`: JetStream's `max_file_store`, in whole GiB (the chart defaults it to the whole PVC, `files/config/jetstream.yaml`). Let S be, with `streamMaxBytes`, the byte limit + the KV buckets' measured bytes + the Raft headroom INFRA-546's sizing states (dispatch://INFRA-546/artifact/plan-md "The size of the byte limit"), in GiB. Default: ⌈S⌉ with `streamMaxBytes`; without it, ⌊0.9 × `diskSizeGb`⌋ (at least 1). Refused below 1, at or above `diskSizeGb`, and, with `streamMaxBytes`, below S (naming both inputs), so a stream at its limit always fits. |
| `diskSizeGb` | `*int`: each pod's PVC size, in whole GiB. Default: with `streamMaxBytes`, ⌈`maxFileStoreGb` / 0.9⌉ and at least `maxFileStoreGb` + 1, so the filesystem's own overhead never fills it; without it, 10. Refused at or below `maxFileStoreGb`. Worked example the sizing test pins: S = 20.3 GiB gives `maxFileStoreGb` 21 and `diskSizeGb` 24; without `streamMaxBytes`, `diskSizeGb` 10 and `maxFileStoreGb` 9. |
| `storageClassName` | `*string`, optional (Autopilot default class when unset). |
| `natsCpu`, `natsMemory` | `*string`, default `1` and `2Gi` (with `streamMaxBytes`, `natsMemory` defaults to the memory INFRA-546 measures for the 72-hour duplicate window at that limit (message count at the limit × memory per retained message id) plus the server's idle memory (a named constant: nats-server v2.15.1's resident memory after the 4.3 cluster forms, measured once and recorded), rounded up to a whole GiB and never below `2Gi`; an explicit value below it is refused naming both inputs); `appQuantity` rules; request = limit. Autopilot floors and ratio refused as `gcp:Dispatch` refuses `appCpu`/`appMemory` (counting the reloader and exporter sidecars' fixed sizes). The sizing constants (mean stored message bytes, memory per retained message id, KV bytes, Raft headroom) are INFRA-546's recorded measurements, each a named constant citing INFRA-546's pull request. |
| `priorityClassName` | `*string`, optional; #2283's rule (refuses a `system-` prefix), looked up with `schedulingv1.GetPriorityClass` so a missing class fails the preview; applied to every pod the component creates. |
| `clientNamespaces` | `[]string`, required, non-empty, each `namespaceRule`, no duplicates: admitted to TCP 4222. |
| `monitorNamespaces` | `[]string`, optional, same rules: admitted to TCP 8222. No rule is written when empty (an empty `from` admits everyone, `dispatch_kube.go:534-535`). |
| `metricsNamespaces` | `[]string`, default `["gmp-system", "gke-gmp-system"]`, same rules: admitted to the exporter's TCP 7777. The implementer cites the GKE document that names the managed collector's namespace on Autopilot in the README; the GMP collector is not on the host network (prometheus-engine `manifests/operator.yaml:335-349`). |
| `users` | `[]gcp:NatsUser`, as `gcp:NatsHub`. |
| `sessionUser` | `*gcp:SessionUser`, as `gcp:NatsHub`. |
| `tailnet` | `*gcp:ClusteredHubTailnet`, optional (2.4): `serviceName` (Tailscale Service name without `svc:`, `hostnameRule`), `tailnetDnsName` (`tailnetDNSNameRule`), `tags` (≥ 1, `tagRule`), `replicas` (`*int`, default 2, ≥ 2), `tailscaleImage` (`imageRule`), `listener` (`gcp:ClusteredHubListener`, required inside `tailnet`: `image` (`imageRule`), `machineId` (`*string`, default `tailnet.serviceName`; `core.CheckMachineID` and the users' durable-collision check), `nkey` (user public key, required), `seedSecretName` (DNS-1123 subdomain) and `seedSecretKey` (`secretKeyRule`) naming an existing Kubernetes Secret in `namespace`, by reference, `allowedHosts` (`core.CheckAllowedHosts`), `cpu`/`memory` (default `500m`/`1Gi`, quantity rules)). |
| `tailnetAuthKey` | `pulumi.StringInput`, `provider:"secret"`: required while `tailnet` is set and refused while it is not (the owned-input rule, `AGENTS.md` "Refusals"); blank and seed refused once it resolves. Must be a reusable, ephemeral, pre-authorized key for the tags (README says so; the broker precedent, agent-infra `broker/frontdoor.go:253-259`). |

Refusals: every refusal is a `core.InputError` naming the input; the component name and every plain string input are checked for an nkey seed first (`seededInput` pattern, `natshub.go:365-404`), Inputs once they resolve. The resolver is a pure `newClusteredHubSettings`, exported to tests as `gcp.ResolveClusteredNatsHub` through `export_test.go`. No `providers.Require` call: the component creates resources only through the provider it builds (`AGENTS.md` "Component-built Kubernetes providers").

### 1.2 Outputs

`serviceUrl` (`nats://<serviceName>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:4222`), `podSelector` (the hub pods' selector labels, so a consumer can point a Service it owns at them), `statefulSetName`; with `tailnet`: `tailnetNatsUrl` (`nats://<tailnet.serviceName>.<tailnetDnsName>:4222`) and `tailnetEnvoyUrl` (`http://…:9020`).

### 1.3 Children

1. `kubernetes:index:Provider` `<name>-kubernetes` (parent: the component). Every child below takes `pulumi.Parent(comp)` and `pulumi.Provider(provider)` (the chart: `pulumi.Providers(provider)`).
2. With `priorityClassName`: the `GetPriorityClass` read (#2283 pattern); the chart and the tailnet Deployment depend on it.
3. `kubernetes:helm.sh/v4:Chart` `<name>`: chart `nats`, version `2.15.1`, repository `https://nats-io.github.io/k8s/helm/charts/`, namespace `namespace`, as constants; values in 2.1; a `Transforms` entry that adds `pulumi.Protect(true)` to the chart's `StatefulSet` (2.3).
4. `NetworkPolicy` `<name>` on the hub pods (2.5).
5. `monitoring.googleapis.com/v1` `PodMonitoring` `<name>` via `apiextensions.NewCustomResource` (the `SecretProviderClass` precedent, `dispatch_kube.go:276-291`): selector = the hub pods' selector labels, endpoint port `prom-metrics`, interval 30s.
6. With `tailnet`: `Secret` `<name>-tailnet-authkey`, `ConfigMap` `<name>-tailnet` (`serve.json` and the advertiser and preStop scripts), `ServiceAccount` `<name>-tailnet` (`automountServiceAccountToken: false`), `Deployment` `<name>-tailnet`, `PodDisruptionBudget` `<name>-tailnet` (`maxUnavailable: 1`).

## 2. Design decisions (each with its reason)

### 2.1 Chart values
- `fullnameOverride: <name>`; `natsBox.enabled: false` (else the chart renders a nats-box Deployment with no budget or priority class, `values.yaml:590-591`, and its test Pod, `templates/tests/request-reply.yaml:1-4`).
- `config.cluster`: `enabled: true`, `replicas: 3`, `noAdvertise: true` (tailnet and in-cluster clients reach the hub only through a Service; advertised pod addresses are unreachable from the tailnet). No route user/password: routes are limited to hub pods by the NetworkPolicy alone (spec bullet 3), which Autopilot's Dataplane V2 enforces; `docs/nats-hub.md` says so, and that the local test runs without the policy.
- `config.jetstream`: `enabled: true`, `fileStore.pvc.size: <diskSizeGb>Gi`, `storageClassName`, `fileStore.maxSize: <maxFileStoreGb>Gi`, `memoryStore.enabled: false`.
- `config.monitor`: enabled on 8222. `config.merge: {"$include": "auth.conf"}`, and `configMap.merge: {data: {"auth.conf": <Render>}}` where `<Render>` is `core.Authorization.Render([]string{confHeader})` of the users built by the same function `gcp:NatsHub` uses (2.6). The chart turns a `$include` key into an include directive and gives the reloader `-config /etc/nats-config/auth.conf` (`templates/_helpers.tpl:256-273`), so a users change rewrites only the ConfigMap and the reloader sends SIGHUP.
- Images: `container.image.fullImageName`, `reloader.image.fullImageName`, `promExporter.image.fullImageName`; `promExporter.enabled: true`, `promExporter.podMonitor.enabled: false` (that is prometheus-operator's kind; GMP needs `PodMonitoring`).
- `container.resources`: requests = limits = `natsCpu`/`natsMemory`; fixed small sizes for reloader and exporter.
- `service`: `enabled: true`, `name: <serviceName>`, only the `nats` port enabled.
- `podTemplate.configChecksumAnnotation: false` (default; stated so a chart default change is caught); `podTemplate.topologySpreadConstraints: {"topology.kubernetes.io/zone": {maxSkew: 1, whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule, minDomains: 3}}` (one pod per zone, hard; `minDomains` stops two pods sharing a zone when only two zones have nodes); `podTemplate.merge.spec.priorityClassName`; `podTemplate.merge.metadata.annotations["envoy-infra.sjawhar.dev/no-auth-user"]` = the session user's public nkey (absent without a session user).
- `podDisruptionBudget.enabled: true` (the chart's own budget is `maxUnavailable: 1`, `files/pod-disruption-budget.yaml`).

### 2.2 The component builds its Kubernetes provider, with mutable ConfigMaps
pulumi-kubernetes v4.34.2 replaces a ConfigMap whose `data` changes unless the provider sets `enableConfigMapMutable` (`provider/pkg/provider/diff.go:23-37`); a named object's replacement deletes it first. A users change would then delete and recreate the hub's ConfigMap, and a pod scheduled in that window fails to mount it. Only a provider the component builds can guarantee the setting, so the component takes `kubeconfig` and builds the provider, as `gcp:Dispatch` builds its own (`dispatch_kube.go:212-214`). A mock test pins `enableConfigMapMutable` and `enableServerSideApply` on that provider and that every child uses it.

### 2.3 The StatefulSet is protected
`volumeClaimTemplates`, `podManagementPolicy`, `serviceName` and `selector` force a StatefulSet's replacement (pulumi-kubernetes v4.34.2 `diff.go:196-205`), which stops all three hub pods at once. A change of `diskSizeGb`, `storageClassName` or a chart bump touching those fields therefore makes `pulumi preview` fail on the protected StatefulSet instead. The README gives the disk-growth procedure (PVC expansion of each claim, then the input) and the unprotect step for a deliberate teardown. Uses Pulumi's own `protect`, as the deployment instructions require.

### 2.4 The tailnet entry is the session listener's workload, and it is optional
The listener serves `/v1` without a credential only on loopback (`cmd/listener/apiauth.go:135-141`), and a Tailscale Service routes to a host, not per port, so each host runs the session listener and serves both ports (spec v2's contract). One Deployment `<name>-tailnet`, one budget. Each pod:
- `tailscale` (containerboot, the `tailscaleImage`): the broker's environment (agent-infra `broker/frontdoor.go:352-397`): `TS_AUTHKEY` from the component's Secret, `TS_AUTH_ONCE=true`, `TS_USERSPACE=true`, `TS_STATE_DIR` on an emptyDir, `TS_KUBE_SECRET=""`, `TS_ACCEPT_DNS=false`, `TS_HOSTNAME` = the pod's name, `TS_EXTRA_ARGS=--advertise-tags=<tags>`, `TS_SERVE_CONFIG=/etc/tailscale/serve.json`, `TS_EXPERIMENTAL_SERVICE_AUTO_ADVERTISEMENT=false`, `TS_ENABLE_HEALTH_CHECK=true`, `TS_LOCAL_ADDR_PORT`, `TS_SOCKET` on an emptyDir the advertiser shares. `serve.json`: `{"Services":{"svc:<tailnet.serviceName>":{"TCP":{"4222":{"TCPForward":"<serviceName>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:4222"},"9020":{"TCPForward":"127.0.0.1:9020"}}}}}`. Startup probe on the local health endpoint. preStop: write the draining file, `tailscale serve drain svc:<name>` (bounded 5 s), `sleep 20`, `tailscale logout` (bounded 5 s), the broker's steps and reasons (`frontdoor_certificate.go:700-790`).
- `listener` (`tailnet.listener.image`): `core.ListenerConfig{MachineID: <machineId>, Port: 9020, ListenHost: "127.0.0.1", AllowedHosts: [core.TailnetHostName(tailnet.serviceName, tailnetDnsName)] + allowedHosts, NATSReplicas: natsReplicas, StreamMaxBytes: streamMaxBytes}.Env([serviceUrl])` plus `NATS_NKEY_SEED_FILE` from the referenced Secret mounted read-only. `ENVOY_ALLOW_REMOTE_NATS=1` comes from `Env` for the in-cluster URL. No `ENVOY_API_TOKEN`. preStop `sleep 25` (the tailscale container's drain 5 s + wait 20 s), so the listener keeps answering while the node drains, then its own ~26 s SIGTERM budget.
- `advertiser` (the `tailscaleImage`, a POSIX sh script from the ConfigMap): every 5 s, advertise `svc:<name>` after two consecutive `wget` 200 answers from `http://127.0.0.1:9020/healthz` (the listener's own NATS check is part of that answer, `cmd/listener/main.go:352-413`); write the ready file only once the node's `service-host` capability lists the Service (Tailscale v1.104.1 `tailcfg.NodeAttrServiceHost`, `tailcfg/tailcfg.go:2556,3112-3125`; the implementer confirms where `tailscale status --json` exposes the self node's capability map in that version and reads it from there); after three consecutive failed health answers, drain and remove the ready file; when advertised and not approved for 120 s, drain, wait, advertise again, doubling the bound (the broker's recovery for a node that advertised before the Service existed, `frontdoor_certificate.go:82-110`); do nothing while the preStop's draining file is newer than the grace period. Readiness probe: `test -e <ready file>`. A pod is Ready only when it serves the tailnet, so the rollout (`maxUnavailable: 0`, `maxSurge: 1`) and the budget count only serving hosts.
- Pod: `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60` (tailscale preStop 30 s + containerboot's 25 s shutdown; listener 25 s + 26 s), a test pins both sums within the grace (`docs/solutions/infra/a-pre-stop-wait-is-paid-out-of-the-pods-grace-…-INFRA-62.md`); zone spread `maxSkew: 1, DoNotSchedule, minDomains: min(replicas, 3)` and node spread `DoNotSchedule`; `priorityClassName`; non-root security context as the images allow (the implementer reads each image's user).
- Coupling stated in `docs/nats-hub.md`: a host whose listener is unhealthy drains both ports, so a listener failure on every pod also takes 4222 off the tailnet; the listener-down alert (INFRA-551) covers it.
- Without `tailnet`, none of these children exist and `tailnetAuthKey` is refused, so a consumer can deploy the hub alone first (see 5, cross-child A).
- These tailnet-host pieces (environment, scripts, budgets) go in their own file, `gcp/tailnet_service.go`, as functions of the Service name and ports, so dispatch://INFRA-560's multi-pod front door can reuse them rather than build a second convention.

### 2.5 NetworkPolicy on the hub pods
Ingress only: TCP 4222 from each `clientNamespaces` namespace (`kubernetes.io/metadata.name`) and from the component's own tailnet pods by pod selector (they forward the tailnet's 4222); TCP 6222 only from the hub pods; TCP 8222 only from `monitorNamespaces`; TCP 7777 only from `metricsNamespaces`. The pod selector is the component's selector-label constant, and the render test (4.2) checks it equals the chart's selector labels.

### 2.6 One users rendering for both hubs
`gcp/natshub.go`'s `authorization()` becomes a function of `(users, listener machine id and nkey, sessionUser)`; `gcp:NatsHub` calls it with `(users, hostname, listener.nkey, sessionUser)` and the clustered hub with `(users, tailnet.listener.machineId, tailnet.listener.nkey, sessionUser)`. `gcp/testdata/cloud-config.golden` and `core/testdata/authorization.golden` stay byte-identical (any change to the cloud-config replaces every VM hub, `AGENTS.md` "Byte-exact texts"). The listener user is named after the machine id with `ListenerPermissions(machineId)`, exactly as the VM names it after its hostname (`natshub.go:530-538`), so with `machineId = envoy-hub` the restored durable `listener-envoy-hub` and the listener's grants carry over the move.

### 2.7 No-credential user changes roll the pods
nats-server v2.15.1 rejects the whole reload when `no_auth_user` changes (`server/reload.go:1967-1977`), so a session-user change must restart each pod. The chart's checksum switch would hash the whole ConfigMap and roll on every users change, so the component sets its own annotation from the session user's key alone (2.1); the StatefulSet's rolling update replaces one pod at a time. Any other users change rewrites only `auth.conf`.

### 2.8 Metrics enough for the two alerts
The exporter runs with the chart's arguments (`-jsz=all -prefix=nats …`, `files/stateful-set/prom-exporter-container.yaml`) and exports one stream series per server holding a copy, labelled `stream_name`, `stream_leader`, `is_stream_leader` (exporter v0.20.2 `collector/jsz.go:94-104,213-266`); it has no replica-currency metric. A stream's copies are therefore counted as the servers reporting it, and a copy is current when its `last_seq` equals the stream's highest. A KV bucket is the stream `KV_<bucket>`, so it is covered. The local test (4.3) shows the exact metric names, three series per R3 stream at rest with equal `last_seq`, two after a kill, and one for an R1 stream; `docs/nats-hub.md` records the names and the PromQL that INFRA-551's alert uses (count of current copies `< 3`). "Pod down" for the hub and the tailnet pods uses Cloud Monitoring's `kubernetes.io/container/*` metrics, as the bridge's alert does (agent-infra `envoy-cluster/bridgealerts.go`); the README says so.

### 2.9 `core.ListenerConfig` gains `NATSReplicas` and `StreamMaxBytes`
They render `ENVOY_NATS_REPLICAS` and `ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES` (read by `packages/envoy/internal/config`, the second added by INFRA-546) only when set above zero, so every existing rendering (`host:Listener`, the AWS components, the VM cloud-config) stays byte-identical. dispatch://INFRA-550 needs the same fields for `gcp:Dispatch`; whichever lands second reuses them.

### 2.10 The hub's grants carry INFRA-546's bucket update grant
The hub's users come from `core`'s permission sets, to which INFRA-546 adds `$JS.API.STREAM.UPDATE.KV_<bucket>` in `bucketPermissions` (dispatch://INFRA-546/artifact/plan-md, decision 5; `core/permissions.go:75-87` grants only `STREAM.INFO` and `STREAM.CREATE` on `KV_<bucket>` today). A test pins that the listener and host users the clustered hub renders hold it for every bucket, so this change merges after INFRA-546 (it also needs INFRA-546's sizing constants and `ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES`).

### 4.2 The chart renders what the values say (`go test -count=1 -tags natslive -run TestClusteredNatsHubChart -v ./gcp/`)
The test checks the vendored archive's SHA-256, runs the component under mocks, writes the chart's `values` input to a file and runs `helm template` at helm v3.20.2 (the version pulumi-kubernetes v4.34.2's provider renders with, its `provider/go.mod:30`), installed by `GOBIN=<temp> go install helm.sh/helm/v3/cmd/helm@v3.20.2` (no replace directives in its go.mod). It asserts: the rendered kinds are exactly StatefulSet, two Services, ConfigMap and PodDisruptionBudget (no nats-box Deployment, no test Pod); the StatefulSet's replicas, spread, `volumeClaimTemplates`, the three containers' images, the reloader's `-config /etc/nats-config/auth.conf`, the session annotation, the priority class, no `checksum/config`; the ConfigMap's `auth.conf` equals `Render` and its `nats.conf` includes `auth.conf` and the cluster and JetStream blocks; the budget is `maxUnavailable: 1`; the component's selector constant equals the StatefulSet's, the budget's and the Service's selectors; the exporter port is named `prom-metrics`. ### 4.3 Three local nats-server processes (`go test -count=1 -tags natslive -run TestClusteredNatsHubCluster -v ./gcp/`)
Binaries installed the same way: `github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2@v2.15.1`, `github.com/nats-io/nack/cmd/nats-server-config-reloader@v0.24.0`, `github.com/nats-io/prometheus-nats-exporter@v0.20.2` (the chart's versions). Each server runs the `nats.conf` and `auth.conf` taken from 4.2's render, with command-line overrides only for what names a pod or a fixed path (`-p`, `-m`, `--cluster nats://127.0.0.1:<port>`, `--routes` to the other two, `-sd`, `-P`, `SERVER_NAME`); `/varz` shows the cluster name from the rendered file. Checks:
- the three form one cluster with a JetStream meta leader; a keyed user (a test seed) connects, a client with no credential becomes the session user and is refused a publish outside `SessionPermissions`;
- a stream at three copies: a publisher sends numbered messages with `Nats-Msg-Id`, retrying each until acknowledged; the stream leader is killed with SIGKILL mid-run; a new leader is elected within 10 s; afterwards the stream holds every acknowledged message exactly once; the killed server restarts on its store and all three copies are current within 30 s;
- the exporter, run with the chart's arguments against each server, reports three `last_seq` series with equal values for the stream at rest, two while one server is down, one for an R1 stream; the test logs the metric names;
- the real reloader runs beside each server with the chart's arguments; a client connected throughout keeps its connection id and zero reconnects while a user is added (it can then connect) and removed (it is then refused), each written as a new `auth.conf` (atomic rename), with every server's PID unchanged;
- a session-user change written the same way is rejected by each server's reload (the log names `no_auth_user`), the previous users stay in force, and a restarted server takes the new session user: the evidence that 2.7's roll is needed.
